Bug_Title: Nullable injected fields and parameters should provide a default value
Bug_Details:
The @Value annotation does not guarantee that the property is defined. Particularly if a field or parameter is annotated as nullable,
it indicates that the developer assumes that the property may be undefined.
An undefined property may lead to runtime exceptions when the Spring framework tries to inject the autowired dependency during bean creation.
This rule raises an issue when a nullable field or parameter is annotated with @Value and no default value is provided.
Bug_Explanation: The code attempts to retrieve a property using properties.getProperty without providing a default value. If 'some.property' is not defined in the properties file, getProperty will return null, which may lead to a NullPointerException or other runtime issues if not handled properly.
Trigger_Explanation: The generated JUnit test case triggers the bug by calling the showBug method of the NullableInjectedFieldDemo class. Since 'some.property' is not defined in the application.properties file, properties.getProperty returns null. This null value is used without a default value, potentially causing a NullPointerException or unexpected behavior in the application.
